This order shall also govern the disposal of W.P. no.19956/2024, W.P. no. 20024/2024, W.P.

no.30481/2024, W.P. no.30574/2024 and W.P.no.30657/2024 having regard to the commonality of the issues involved.
2. For the sake of convenience, the facts as narrated in Writ Petition No.19395 of 2024 are being taken into consideration.

3. This petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been filed by the petitioners,
seeking the following reliefs:-
4 WP-30657-2024 "7
( a) This petition may kindly be allowed with costs.
(b) The impugned award dated 12.3.2024 and amended award dated 10.06.2024 may kindly be set aside.

(c) The Government respondents may kindly be directed to comply with provisions relating to social impact assessment and rehabilitation and resettlement for the affected families before displacing the affected families from the land subjected to acquisition.

(d) Issue such other orders, writ, and direction as this Hon'ble Court deems fit in the interest of justice in favour of the petitioner."
4.

The petitioners, who are the resident of Takiya Mazjid, Nizamuddin colony, Jaisinghpura, Ujjain and the adjacent area, are aggrieved of the award dated 12.3.2024, as also the amended Award dated 10.06.2024, passed by the respondent no.3/District Collector, Ujjain Cum-Land Acquisition Officer,
District-Ujjain (M.P.) under the provisions of Section 40?? of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act of 2013").
5. The aforesaid Award has been challenged by the petitioners on the ground that the respondents have not adhered to the mandatory provisions of the Act of 2013, especially the preparation of social impact assessment study as has been provided under Sections 4 to 8 of the Act of 2013.

It is also submitted that despite invoking Section 40 of the Act, its provisions have not been complied with,
and thus, the 'extension' as provided under Section 9 from preparation of Social Impact assessment is not available to the respondents.
It is also submitted that the provisions of Sections 31 and onwards as provided under Chapter V and VI of the Act of 2013 have also not been complied with.

6 . Counsel for the petitioners has also submitted that the 5 WP-30657-2024 petitioners have not been given any compensation, and the respondents are bent upon take possession of their premises without following the due procedure as provided under the Act of 2013.

Counsel has further submitted that although the petitioners are also not opposed to the acquisition of land but, for that Mohd. Raees vs State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141078817/
3 the respondents ought to have complied with the mandatory provisions of the Act of 2013 so as to grant proper compensation, rehabilitation and resettlement to the petitioners.
7.

sentences.text: A reply to the petition has also been filed by the respondent/State, and it is stated that although initially the land was supposed to be acquired while invoking Section 40 of the Act of 2013, which provides for special powers in case of urgency to acquire land in certain cases.

However, the land was not acquired within 48 hours as the petitioners have been allowed to remain in their respective premises, although the compensation has already been provided to all the settlers.

It is submitted that out of 250 families, more than 230 families have already vacated the premises, and 20 families who have still remained in their premises, are the persons who have not provided their bank account number to facilitate the payment of compensation.
8. It is also submitted that otherwise also the title documents have also not been provided to the respondents to verify the right of claim of such persons.

9. Counsel for the respondent has also submitted that the only dispute between the parties is in respect of compensation which can be challenged by the petitioners under Section 64 of the Act of 2013, and thus, 6 WP-30657-2024 it is submitted that on account of availability of statutory remedy available to the petitioners, no case for interference is made out as the petition is premature.

It is also submitted that the project report of development which is required for the development of the area for which the present writ petition is filed, is also annexed and marked as A/1 and the project report of rope- way is annexed and marked as Annexure A/2.
10.

In rebuttal, counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the provisions of Section 40 of the Act of the Act of 2013 have not been complied with by the respondents as they were required to comply with the provisions as provided under Section 4 onwards.
Thus, it is submitted that the alternative remedy is not efficacious, as the respondents have not taken care of the rehabilitation of the petitioners.
It is also submitted that the reference authority has no jurisdiction to examine the legality or non- compliance of the mandatory provisions, as its jurisdiction is confined only to the compensation.

11. Heard the learned counsel for the parties, and also perused the record.
12.
On perusal of the record, it is found that the land has been acquired for the construction of second phase of Mahakal-Lok.
The Notification regarding which has also been published for the public on 15.3.2024, giving all the details of the proposed construction, which include the construction of rope-way also.

13. According to the respondents, the amount of compensation of the building has already been deposited and the compensation of the land is 7 WP-30657-2024 yet to be deposited but, the same could not be done as the possession was not handed-over to the respondents.

14. The respondents' further contention is that pillar no.11 is to be constructed for the ropeway from railway station to Mahakaal-Mandir but, on account of the stay order, the project is being delayed.

4 is also submitted that the compensation has already been enhanced, as per the Act of 2013, which is not disputed by the petitioners.

sentences.text: 15. The respondents have also taken a plea that in the Municipal record and the revenue records, the names of residents are not mentioned and the mutation has not taken place, on that count, it was asked from the residents if they have any title document, they can disclose the same to the authorities so that the compensation of the land can be made to their individual account, but the same has not been done by the petitioners and instead they have directly challenged the award before this Court.

16. It is also found that the petitioners are aggrieved of the Award dated 12.03.2024, which has been amended on 10.06.2024 by the District Collector-cum-Land Acquisition Officer, which, for all the practical purposes is an Award passed under Section 37 or s.40 of the Act of 2013, which can only be challenged by way of reference to the competent authority under Section 64 of the Act of 2013,
which provides that any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Authority, as the case may be, whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the person to 8 WP-30657-2024 whom it is payable, the rights of Rehabilitation and Resettlement under Chapters V and VI or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.
It is also found that Section 64 has no exclusion clause which may indicate that any particular ground of fact and law cannot also be raised before the Authority.

On the contrary, this court also finds that the language used u/s.64 is couched in such a manner so as to leave no manner of doubt that it covers all the grounds available to any person aggrieved of an award either passed u/s.37 or Section 40 of the Act of 2015 both of which fall under Chapter V of the same.

17. In such circumstances, when the petitioners have not disclosed in their petition regarding the availability of the alternative remedy, this Court is not inclined to exercise its extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, especially when there is no challenge to the Award by the other persons who have already accepted the award.
18. In view of the same, the petition fails and is hereby dismissed.
However, with a liberty reserved to the petitioners to take recourse of the remedy available to them under law.

It is directed that if the petitioners approach the Authority within a further period of thirty (30) days from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order, the same shall be decided by the Authority, in accordance with law, without raising any objection regarding the limitation.
19. It is made clear that this court has not reflected upon the merits of the case.
20. With the aforesaid, all the petitions stand disposed of.
